rv.q: What makes Attendant worth seeing, despite its obvious rough patches, is that Kelly is reaching toward something larger than a Vegas blackmail caper.
Boldly (if shaggily) written and unevenly acted, this Vegas caper is that rarest of off-off-Broadway wonders: a play heterosexual men can truly enjoy.

At more than two hours (including intermission), Attendant is too long and feels far out of time; it starts slowly, has a more gripping middle section, but then devolves into convoluted plot devices and huge plot holes.

cn.t: Critics find this Las Vegas-set thriller imperfect but compelling, with strong performances and resourceful staging elevating a story of desperation and betrayal that doesn't fully deliver on its premise.
